REDACT-001/F1.why: The audit-row test checks action, scope and rule_count and never checks `content`; a row carrying the raw input passes. The exhibit.

REDACT-001/F2.why: Verified by hand 2026-09-17 with `python -m unittest`, reading its exit code, not TestGuard's reporter: with masking skipped, two of four tests fail (the secret is present, and no audit row is written).

REDACT-001/F3.why: Verified by hand 2026-09-17 with `python -m unittest`, reading its exit code, not TestGuard's reporter: with the content key removed, all four tests pass. The assertions name three keys and a row with no content at all is indistinguishable from a correct one.

REDACT-002/F1.why: Verified by hand 2026-09-17 with `python -m unittest`, reading its exit code, not TestGuard's reporter: re-raising re.error makes compile_rules propagate; the invalid-pattern test errors (1 of 4). An exception raised in the test body is the suite rejecting the behaviour, exactly as it is under jest.

REDACT-003/F1.why: No test exercises a missing scope; the fail-closed guard is undefended.

REDACT-004/F1.why: Verified by hand 2026-09-17 with `python -m unittest`, reading its exit code, not TestGuard's reporter: the process does not finish. Python has no per-test timeout without a plugin, so the run ends at TestGuard's wall-clock budget. A timeout is not an assertion failure and is not a kill.

REDACT-005/F1.why: The find string is not present in the source (0 hits).

REDACT-005/F2.why: `return None` occurs in find_rule and in scope_of (2 hits); expectHits is 1.

REDACT-006/F1.why: Verified by hand 2026-09-17 with `python -m unittest`, reading its exit code, not TestGuard's reporter: the unbalanced parenthesis makes demo/redact.py unimportable, so the test module fails to collect. A SyntaxError reaches TestGuard as a collection error, never as a kill.

REDACT-007/F1.why: Verified by hand 2026-09-17 with `python -m unittest`, reading its exit code, not TestGuard's reporter: mask(text, []) masks nothing, so no audit row is written and the output still contains the secret: two of four tests fail.

EXPORT-001/F1.why: tests/test_export.py does not exist; no defender resolves.

EXPORT-002/F1.why: The only test that imports demo.export patches the module itself and never asserts on it. A patch of the whole module cannot detect a fault in it, so discovery excludes the file: no defender, and the evidence lists it under defenders.mocking with a mocked-never-asserted signal.

FLAKY-001/F1.why: tests/test_flaky.py fails on every odd run; the baseline is not green N/N, so no verdict about the fault is possible.

DISCOVER-001/F1.why: No defendedBy. Defenders are discovered by Python module name: tests/test_redact.py and tests/test_patched.py both import demo.redact, and verified by hand 2026-09-17 with `python -m unittest`, reading its exit code, not testguard's reporter: removing the substitution fails every test in both.

PATCHED-001/F1.why: The defender patches demo.redact.compile_rules but exercises mask for real, so it is a defender and it notices: verified by hand 2026-09-17 with `python -m unittest`, reading its exit code, not testguard's reporter: collapsing each match to one asterisk fails its assertion. The JavaScript rule — drop any file that mocks the target — would have reported this claim as nocover. The evidence records target-attribute-patched instead.

UNREACHED-001/F1.why: The declared defender never imports demo.orphan, so nothing it asserts could detect this fault. The tests are not blind to the fault; they never reach it. Recorded as detail.targetNotImported, which is what distinguishes this from a real survivor.
